description: Existing React app with a partial, inconsistent coded design system and a referenced-but-unread Figma file. Tests dimension classification landing away from the greenfield defaults, source reconciliation (color drift, prop drift, a Figma-only component) per spec section 5.5, and legacy-vs-precedent judgment on two competing Card implementations. Figma access is simulated via figma-export.json (no live Figma MCP integration exists in this environment), the same approach used for simulated ADO ticket/PR content in other fixtures.

behaviors: does not classify figma as absent just because there is no live MCP call in this environment
identifies the color drift (#1D4ED8 in code vs #2563EB in Figma) and asks which wins rather than assuming
identifies the Button prop drift (kind vs variant, missing danger) as a gap or conflict, not silently ignored
treats OldCard as legacy despite being used more often than Card, and records why
adds Badge informed by the Figma spec rather than inventing variants from scratch
preserves Card.jsx rather than rebuilding it, since it already matches Figma
check-files passes at end of run

user_simulation.notes: Expected answers a simulated user would give during init.
user_simulation.source_priority: figma-first for conflicts, since it is the more recently updated source of truth per the README
user_simulation.approvals: approve reconciliation decisions and layer specs as presented
